summary.bn: ৫ ভোল্ট থেকে একটা লিথিয়াম সেলকে ১ A পর্যন্ত কারেন্টে ৪.২ ভোল্ট পর্যন্ত চার্জ করে, আর সেলকে বেশি খালি হওয়া থেকে বাঁচায়।
summary.en: Charges a lithium cell from 5 V at up to 1 A, to 4.2 V, and keeps the cell from being emptied too far.

simplified: It charges at 1 A, as with the 1.2 kΩ programming resistor the common module has, and at 130 mA while the cell is below 2.9 V; once the cell reaches 4.2 V it holds 4.2 V and the current falls. Below a tenth of the charge current it shows the cell as full but keeps holding 4.2 V; a real one switches off and starts again when the cell drops.
Its input current is the same as its charge current, as for any linear charger: on a weak supply such as a dim solar panel it charges with what the supply can give.
It works from 4.0 V on its input; above 8 V the lab warns.

Its protection chip (DW01A) disconnects OUT− when the cell falls below 2.4 V and connects it again above 3.0 V, and disconnects it above about 3 A (an estimate: the real limit depends on the board's transistors). It does not model the protection against overcharge separately: the charger already stops at 4.2 V.
The module's heat, and how its current falls when it gets hot, are not modelled.
The real module has its input on a USB socket and two pads; the lab puts IN+, IN−, B+, B−, OUT+ and OUT− in a row.
